newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland irked by Paris egg-throwing at president.
newsitem.headline: Poland irked by Paris egg-throwing at president.

text.p: Poland is concerned that its president's security came under threat when four rightist Poles got close enough to fling eggs at him during a visit to Paris, the government's spokewoman said on Monday.
"Judging from the information we have, not everything was done to ensure proper security for the president," spokeswoman Aleksandra Jakubowska told a news briefing.
"If eggs could reach (the president), so could...stones, if not hand grenades," Jakubowska said.
She said it was too early to say whether Poland's foreign ministry would formally protest to France over the security provided for President Aleksander Kwasniewski.
The government would discuss the issue on Tuesday.
Kwasniewski, a former communist turned social democrat, and wife Jolanta were entering a Paris theatre to attend a concert on Sunday when the protesters threw the eggs.
They missed Kwasniewski, but Polish news media reported that two of his aides were hit and were planning civil lawsuits against their attackers, who were detained by police.
Presidential spokesman Antoni Styrczula was earlier quoted by private Radio Zet as saying Poland was mulling a diplomatic note to the French government over the incident.
Two small, virtually unknown rightist groups held a news conference to say that their members travelled to Paris specifically to hurl eggs at Kwasniewski.

"We express solidarity with our colleagues arrested in France and we will stand in their defence using all legal means," PAP news agency quoted the leader of one group, Piotr Lisiewicz, as telling reporters in the western city of Poznan.

Kwasniewski, in office since 1995, and his political allies from the co-ruling ex-communist Democratic Left Alliance, are often heckled during public appearances in Poland by rightists, who say their involvement in the old regime before 1989 should disqualify them from politics.
Mainstream right and centre opposition parties, which hope to defeat the ex-communists in this year's parliamentary elections, mostly distance themselves from such incidents.

Kwasniewski, due to return to Warsaw late on Monday, met his counterpart Jacques Chirac earlier in the day and received fresh confirmation of France's support for Poland's efforts to quickly join NATO and the European Union.
